subject: Private endpoint outbound assertion & firewall Q&A

Subject: Private deployment - outbound constraints, allowlist needs

Mateo,

Thanks for taking this. As part of our on‑prem proof of concept we need a concise spec we can hand to our NetOps team to configure the perimeter firewall and allowlist. Can you confirm the following items for Redwood's private endpoint (VPC/on‑prem) model?

1) Authoritative egress IPs (CSV preferred) and whether they are static per‑tenant or ephemeral.
2) Required outbound ports/protocols (including control plane vs model/data plane differences).
3) FQDNs that must be resolvable (for cloud telemetry, model updates, package fetches) and whether DNS binding is acceptable instead of IPs.
4) Any TLS/mTLS expectations (SNI, client certs, headers).
5) Expected IP rotation cadence and a notification mechanism if IPs change.
6) Audit/attestation we can provide to our security team (evidence package, contact for SOC2 questions).

We want to validate this week and schedule a short test cutover next Wed evening. If you can send a single document and attach a CSV of IPs that would be ideal.

Thanks — Sophie
Sophie Reed
Senior Information Security Manager
Halcyon Bank

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Private deployment - outbound constraints, allowlist needs

Sophie — great questions. High level summary first, then the attachments and next steps below.

Summary (short):
- Redwood supports three egress modes for private endpoints:
  a) Per‑tenant static IP blocks (recommended for strict allowlist setups)
  b) Ephemeral NAT with signed origin assertion (for customers who prefer DNS + origin assertion)
  c) Customer‑provided outbound proxy (we can route through your proxy if you prefer)
- Control plane (management/health) and data plane (inference traffic) are separate; both require outbound HTTPS but to different hostnames.
- TLS is required for all traffic. mTLS is available for Dedicated Private installs by request; typically not required for quick POCs.

Attachments I sent: redwood-egress-ip-list.csv (authoritative IPs for the mode we discussed) and firewall-sample-policy.yaml (example rules you can drop into your firewall config).

Key details (please pass to NetOps):
- Authoritative outbound IPs: see attached CSV. For the static mode, these are stable /29–/24 ranges; for ephemeral mode the attachment includes the assertion endpoints and DNS entries.
- Ports and protocols:
  * 443/tcp outbound to data plane (model inference endpoints)
  * 443/tcp outbound to control.redwood.ai (control plane, telemetry, heartbeats)
  * 443/tcp outbound to updates.redwood.ai (model/agent fetches)
  * 853/udp (optional) for DoT if you manage DNS over TLS internally
- FQDNs recommended to allow (DNS is acceptable for some services):
  * data-*.redwood.ai (inference endpoints)
  * control.redwood.ai
  * updates.redwood.ai
  * telemetry.redwood.ai (ingest for diagnostic telemetry; can be disabled per contract)
- Origin assertion: when using ephemeral IPs we provide an Origin Assertion header (X-Redwood-Origin: <customer-id‑signature>) which you can validate at proxy/firewall level.
- mTLS: available for Dedicated/Private customers on request — requires cert exchange and CA pin.
- Rotation & notifications: static mode = low rotation; ephemeral mode = rotated daily by default. We publish a signed CSV and push a webhook to your NetOps endpoint and send an automated email to the security contact on rotation.
- Evidence & compliance: we can provide an evidence bundle (SOC2 summary, IP allocation manifest, firewall rule snippets, and a signed attestation). If you want that package we will upload it to the DocuSign/secure share after your PO.

Next steps we propose:
1) NetOps consumes redwood-egress-ip-list.csv and applies the rules from firewall-sample-policy.yaml in a staging ACL.
2) Halcyon runs a short functional test window (30 minutes) using our ephemeral mode; we will provide test tokens and an A/B fallback to hosted endpoints.
3) If staging passes, sign the attestation and schedule production cutover (we recommend a 2‑hour maintenance window).

I’ve CC'd Marissa from Ops so we can schedule the cutover. If you'd like mTLS we can scope that in parallel.

— Mateo Alvarez
Senior Solutions Architect, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Attachments:

- firewall-sample-policy.yaml (example ACL rules and pseudo‑code)

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Private deployment - outbound constraints, allowlist needs (technical addendum)

Adding a few technical clarifications from the runtime/network team so NetOps has everything in one place.

1) Control plane vs Data plane specifics:
   - Control plane: TLS 443 to control.redwood.ai. Uses API tokens; expects standard SNI for routing. IPs used are drawn from the attached control plane block in redwood-egress-ip-list.csv.
   - Data plane: TLS 443 to data-<region>.redwood.ai (region-aware). For POC you can allow data-*.redwood.ai.

2) Headers & identity:
   - When ephemeral NAT is used we include header X-Redwood-Client-ID and X-Redwood-Origin for origin assertion. If you validate via header, ensure your proxy preserves those headers to downstream logging.
   - We do not recommend relying solely on source IP for authentication when ephemeral mode is used; use header assertion + TLS.

3) mTLS & cert pinning:
   - mTLS is optional. If Halcyon requires mTLS for both control and data planes, we will coordinate cert exchange and provide CA cert bundles.

4) IP rotation cadence & evidence:
   - Ephemeral: daily rotation by default; we can change cadence to weekly on request.
   - Static: changes only on major infra updates; we provide 30 days' notice via signed CSV and webhook.

5) Telemetry & logging endpoints:
   - If you accept telemetry, telemetry.redwood.ai will receive health pings and anonymized metrics. This can be disabled.

6) Test guidance:
   - For initial validation open 443 outbound to the attached IP ranges and allow DNS resolution for data-*.redwood.ai. Use our staging tokens (sent in a separate secure message) and run 50 concurrent inference requests to validate throughput and expected timeouts.

I also attached an "allowlist-evidence-checklist.pdf" that contains the items our security team typically provides (IP manifest, signed attestation, SOC2 pointer, example firewall logs).

David Kim
Principal Network Engineer
Redwood Inference
